text:
jane_cust: Hey team, mid-demo panic — our integration started returning 429s ~10m ago and the client demo is in 30 minutes. We're using the free tier API key (monthly free credits) and doing a bulk embeddings ingest (parallel, ~50 req/s). Can someone triage? Sample error: `HTTP 429: rate_limit_exceeded`.

alex_support: Sorry you're hitting this, @jane_cust. Can you paste the root request pattern and an example curl or client snippet? Also which endpoint (embeddings/generate/chat)? Are you using the same API key for all workers?

jane_cust: embeddings endpoint (`/v1/embeddings`) — we spawn 10 workers each doing ~5 concurrent requests. Here's a simplified curl we're running in parallel:```bash
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -s -X POST 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":"some long text blob"}' 
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings &
done
wait
```
Response sample: `{"error": {"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 15s."}}`

alex_support: Thanks. Can you confirm the org/account ID? I want to check quota windows. If you're on the free tier, there are both per-minute request and token-based per-month caps — burst allowance is limited.

ops-bot: Notification: org 0xafe3f exhausted daily request burst window (policy: free-tier-burst).

alex_support: Ops bot shows you're hitting the free-tier burst cap. Two short-term paths: 1) implement immediate client-side backoff + limit concurrency to 2 workers to avoid 429s for the demo, or 2) we can request a short-lived temporary burst exception (sales approval required) to raise concurrent throughput for up to 1 hour. Which do you prefer?

jane_cust: Demo is scheduled with investors; we need minimal changes on our side. Can you ask sales for a temporary uplift for 1 hour? We'll sign up for paid if needed afterwards.

maria_sales: @alex_support looping in — we can consider a 1-hour demo burst if compliance/billing OK. What's the org email and would they be willing to add a card now? For billing, we typically require a paid billing method for exceptions; if they can add a card we can do a reversible short-term limit bump.

alex_support: Org email is team@example-startup.com (shared by @jane_cust). Do you want me to open the exception request ticket with the required fields? Also pinging @jing_dev for any runtime constraints if we flip a temporary policy flag.

jing_dev: Quick note from runtime: we enforce two buckets — requests-per-second (RPS) and tokens-per-minute (TPM) — plus a free-tier burst window that smooths short spikes. We can flip an org-level `demo_burst` flag to allow higher short-term RPS, but only if billing/sales confirm. Risk: it will increase unit spend; no code changes required. Alternative: sample-level batching (send multiple items in one embeddings call) would massively reduce RPS.

jane_cust: Batching is non-trivial for their demo flow, so temporary lift is preferred.

maria_sales: OK — can you confirm dollar tolerance? We can provision a 1-hour uplift capped at $200 and require a card on file. If they accept, I can approve internally and have ops flip the flag. @alex_support can you confirm the org id & owner email to attach to the request?

alex_support: Org ID: 0xafe3f. Owner email: billing+team@example-startup.com. I'll send the formal exception request now.

alex_support: (to ops) Request: org 0xafe3f, temporary demo uplift 1 hour, cap $200, requested by customer for investor demo. Please confirm and flip `demo_burst` if approved.

ops-bot: Ticket created: EXC-2026-119. Assigned to ops-runbooks.

ops-bot: Approval needed from billing.

maria_sales: I've ack'd the ticket and scheduled a 1-hour uplift contingent on card on file. @jane_cust please add a card to the org billing page and reply here when done. :thumbsup:

jane_cust: Card added. I also dropped a note in the billing portal with the demo window (starts in 20 minutes).

ops-bot: Change approved. Toggling `demo_burst` for org 0xafe3f for 3600s.

ops-bot: Change applied. Org 0xafe3f new temporary RPS limit: 60 (was 10). TPM unchanged.

alex_support: Uplift applied. You should be able to retry now — but please still use conservative retries/backoff. If you still see 429s, reduce concurrency to 4 and add 2s jitter.

jane_cust: Retried and it looks good — embeddings complete and demo proceeds. Huge thanks!

alex_support: Great. Follow-ups: 1) Sales to follow up on paid plan conversion, 2) Dev note from @jing_dev about batching and backoff best practices, 3) We'll close EXC-2026-119 after billing reconciliation.

jing_dev: I'll add a short doc with recommended patterns: batching, exponential backoff (with full jitter), and client-side rate limiting. Quick example for exponential backoff pseudocode:```python
for attempt in range(max_retries):
  try:
    res = client.embeddings.create(...)
    break
  except RateLimitError:
    sleep = base * (2 ** attempt) + random.random()
    time.sleep(min(sleep, max_sleep))
```

maria_sales: I'll convert the conversation to a handoff and include the $200 demo uplift note. @jane_cust I'll reach out about a tailored Dedicated or Reserved plan if you want predictable throughput.

jane_cust: Appreciate the fast help, everyone. Closing on our side.

alex_support: Marking thread resolved. If anything else pops up, reopen or ping #support. :white_check_mark:
